subject: host-effect-authorization.v2
protocol: Independent review under D-000; refute not confirm; successor to v1 REJECT
summary: My v1 blocker is genuinely repaired, not relabelled. D-032 assigned this contract exactly one question and v2 answers it with a decision rule — the execution side is the process that opens the socket, not who named the consent — then applies it in three clauses and four named preview paths, and kills the unless-bypass outright at ES-3. All three of my v1 advisories are repaired, one of them past what I asked. I attacked every axis the prompt names and found no blocker. The fail-closed rule is now a six-conjunct AND with the v1 Boolean defect named and repaired in the artifact's own bytes; FC-C1 forecloses self-bootstrapping and FC-C4 forecloses this contract standing as its own product admission. The seven join blockers are individually named with BLK-1 through BLK-4 held STILL-ROUTED and BLK-3 explicitly not discharged by the vocabulary's existence. CA-3 now carries a per-subtype product-admission layer with admission evidence recorded ABSENT or DEFERRED. Nothing is minted: the artifact's own claim that its sole concrete PT-* identifier is the out-of-scope PT-NET-EGRESS is exactly true at seven occurrences, and both uses of SATISFIED are negative. Two advisories remain, both about disclosure rather than substance.

findings.claim: doctorV4ReservedPoint names doctor v4's two-part reservation condition and dispositions only one half. DR-105 has not closed, and the artifact does not state why that conjunct no longer binds the host half of the member it is activating.
findings.evidence: Measured in doctor-contract.v4.json at df2e7175…, the effectOutcome member is defined with the key 'shapeUntilTheActorDecisionAndDr105Close' and the value 'RESERVED BINDING POINT: { reserved: true, ridesOn: ["DR-105"], conditionedOn: "the ACTOR decision at ID-DEP-12" }'. The key name states a conjunction: the shape holds until the actor decision AND DR-105 close. v2's doctorV4ReservedPoint reads 'doctor v4 reserved effectOutcome on DR-105 and the actor decision. D-032 made the actor decision (Option B) and commissioned this contract to supply the host vocabulary. This artifact is that supply.' It names both conjuncts in its first sentence and then discharges only the actor one. DR-105 has not closed: file 08 at 877e36d3 records DR-105 as OPEN and its cell ends 'This row is not SATISFIED', with permission v1 REJECTED at 3 blockers and the join still INCOHERENT at 7. A sound argument for proceeding is available and is implied by the artifact's own architecture — under Option B host acts are outside DR-105, so DR-105's closure governs the component half of the member and not the host half — but the artifact does not make it. This matters because the binding it asserts is strong: normativeBinding makes an unpopulated effectOutcome unlawful for a host attempt after recording, which reverses doctor v4's current interim rule that such a record is 'written with the reserved effectOutcome member unpopulated and a non-null residual limitation saying so'. The artifact is careful elsewhere about exactly this kind of cross-artifact reach — it states 'It does not amend doctor v4's header' and leaves a later doctor successor to restate the point — so the missing half-sentence is an omission in an otherwise disciplined passage rather than an overreach.
findings.proposedFix: Add one sentence to doctorV4ReservedPoint: DR-105's closure conditions the component half of the member; under D-032 Option B host acts are outside DR-105, so the host half does not wait on it, and doctor v4's unpopulated-plus-residual interim rule continues to govern component records and host records made before this contract is recorded.

findings.claim: The D-032 sectionSha256 is correct and I reproduced it, but the selector states no extraction rule, so the pin is reproducible only by search — and the most natural mechanical reading yields a different digest.
findings.evidence: governingDecisions.D-032 pins sectionSha256 00085513a0551aded3b1996bf448c42f16265ce0a4409eb5d926108d1bd63367 with selector '## D-032 — DR-105 / DR-114 actor scope (Option B + measured tails)'. A heading string fixes where a section starts and not where it ends. I could not reproduce the digest from the obvious rule: extracting from that heading to the next '## ' heading yields 8d31de01c4408a7a280e619186d98dc0931ee890eee1a45a04aeeb1a08ec71f1, and dropping the horizontal-rule line yields 7df861234267b181324c271ec8474863558f1c6d76026ab37614174bcc265197. Neither matches. I then searched the range space — three candidate start lines against sixteen candidate end lines — and the claimed digest reproduces exactly at lines 1621 through 1654, which is the heading through the last content line, excluding the trailing separator. So the pin is honest and the bytes are right; what is missing is the rule that makes it checkable without a search. This is worth recording precisely because section pinning is the corpus's own recommended successor to whole-document pins, adopted here for the first time in this artifact class: the practice is only better than a whole-file pin if the extraction is deterministic for the next reader.
findings.proposedFix: State the extraction rule alongside the selector, for example: 'section = the heading line through the last line before the next horizontal rule, excluding that rule; lines 1621-1654 at the pinned whole-file digest.' Line numbers alone would strand on the next register edit, so the rule should be stated in terms of delimiters with the line range given as a convenience.

predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA1-B1: REPAIRED — verified, and this is the repair that lifts the v1 REJECT. v1 returned D-032's single assignment marked 'UNSETTLED which slice-1 doctor egress is host vs component' with no owner and no route. v2's slice1EgressExecutionSide opens by quoting the assignment and answering it: 'This artifact is that contract. The assignment is answered here. It is not returned UNSETTLED.' It then supplies a decision rule — 'The execution side is the process that opens the socket, not who named the consent' — and applies it in three clauses: ES-1 puts every send or receive by the doctor process itself at HOST CA-4; ES-2 puts every send or receive by a process doctor spawned at component-originated egress, 'exclusively DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS. This contract cannot authorize it. Host consent cannot substitute'; ES-3 makes an unnamed doctor-process socket UNCLASSIFIED and UNEXERCISABLE 'regardless of consent, regardless of this contract's recording, and regardless of an authorization record. No unless-bypass exists.' Four named architecture-preview paths then carry an executionSide and a productAdmission standing each. That is a settled rule with its consequences worked through, not a deferral.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA1-A1: REPAIRED — joinBlockerDisposition names all seven blockers where v1 named none; the substring 'BLK-' occurred zero times in v1. BLK-1 through BLK-4 are STILL-ROUTED with an answeredAt pointer each, and the source line states 'This artifact names them. It discharges none of them.' BLK-3's state is the one I would have attacked and it forecloses the attack: 'The three members exist and are bound to consentRecords[].effectOutcome. Existence of the vocabulary does not discharge the blocker.' BLK-5, BLK-6 and BLK-7 are recorded as already disposed by adopted D-032 and not reopened. whatThisDoesNotDo repeats the non-discharge for BLK-1, BLK-2, BLK-3 and BLK-4.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA1-A2: REPAIRED, and exceeded. I asked for FC-NOT-SUFFICIENT covering the CA-2 and CA-1 instances. The artifact adds that class with all three instances — CA-2 against DR-119, CA-1 against DR-G21, KEYCHAIN against DR-108 — and adds three further classes I did not ask for that decompose the fail-closed conjunction directly: FC-CONSENT-WITHOUT-CONTRACT, FC-CONTRACT-WITHOUT-CONSENT, and FC-CONSENT-CONTRACT-WITHOUT-PRODUCT-ADMISSION, the last covering 'CA-2 without DR-119, CA-1 without DR-G21, and each UNOWNED-FOR-ADMISSION CA-3 subtype'. FC-OUTCOME is also strengthened to fail a fixture that encodes the outcome on execution, result, residualLimitation or a check status, or that leaves effectOutcome unpopulated on an attempted host act after recording.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA1-A3: REPAIRED, and exceeded. v1 recorded D-032 as the bare string 'COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-032 ADOPTED' with no digest. v2's recordedInputs pins COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 54d34099… plus a separate D-032-section digest, governingDecisions.D-032 adds a selector, a sectionSha256 and eleven property pins, and a remeasurementClause is present stating that the whole-file pin 'supports only the D-032 section named at governingDecisions.D-032.selector / sectionSha256' and that doctor v4, permission v1 and the join review are pinned 'as environment and as predecessor inputs, not as applied authority'. The residual concerns the section pin's extraction rule and is raised at IR-HEA2-A2.
predecessorFindingVerification.HAE-CX-01..05 and HAE-ADV-01: NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIABLE AS TO THE FINDING TEXT — I have not read the Codex v1 verdict at any point. predecessorVerdictFindings records all five Codex blockers plus an advisory as REPAIRED with locations, and I verified that the repairs at those locations exist and are substantive: failClosed and layers carry a six-conjunct rule with the v1 Boolean defect named; authorizationRecord and effectCommit carry a closed member schema and per-class commit boundaries; outcomeVocabulary carries the serialization binding; slice1EgressExecutionSide carries the settled rule; coveredActs.CA-3 carries per-subtype product-admission standing. I confirm the repairs are present and responsive to the axes the review prompt names; I cannot confirm they discharge findings whose wording I have never seen.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 1f58494a2532f4d631f7135e497d09bfc09f3b02cd040ffa3a9190f3d6814c2a both times. No drift.

Fail-closed is no longer a Boolean defect, and the artifact says so at bytes. rulePositive reads 'An in-scope host act is exercisable only when every required condition below is true… Denial is not (!consent && !instance)'; boolean reads 'exercisable iff FC-C1 AND FC-C2 AND FC-C3 AND FC-C4 AND FC-C5 AND FC-C6. Absence of any conjunct denies'; and v1DefectRepaired quotes the v1 rule and states what still denies. Two conjuncts do structural work worth naming: FC-C1 forecloses self-bootstrapping — 'This file existing is not that recording' — and FC-C4 forecloses this contract standing as its own product admission — 'This contract is never that evidence'. FC-C5 makes UNCLASSIFIED unexercisable irrespective of everything else.

The three-layer separation is explicit at layers: design contract, per-invocation authorization record, and product admission, with the design contract marked 'Necessary. Not sufficient' and becoming live only on a joint-owner recording following the D-035 pattern.

The authorization-record schema exists and is closed. authorizationRecord.closedMembers carries id, actor, actionClass, actionSubtype, invocationId, checkIds, resourceScope, toolIdentity and further members, with actor closed to HOST-UNDER-INSTRUCTION, actionClass closed to the four families, and CA-3/CA-4 subtypes closed to their enumerations. Two clauses are worth recording: id is explicitly 'Not a RunId, EvidenceDigest, grant-generation id, or any DR-006 recipe. This contract mints no identity recipe', and resourceScope is 'Never a glob, never "*", never "any", never empty-meaning-all'. The nullWhen rule makes an unnamed CA-3 or CA-4 subtype UNCLASSIFIED and DENIED, which is the same fail-closed direction as ES-3.

Outcomes are bound to doctor v4's member, and the citation resolves. outcomeVocabulary.serialization names field consentRecords[].effectOutcome. I located the member in doctor v4: it exists at /consentModel/mandatoryPostReport/recordMembers/10, required: true. The artifact's shorthand 'mandatoryPostReport.recordMembers effectOutcome' omits the consentModel prefix, but that shorthand is doctor v4's own — v4's reviewGuidance itself says 'See mandatoryPostReport.recordMembers `effectOutcome`' — so it is the source's convention and not a defect. The normativeBinding forbids four specific substitutions by name: residualLimitation prose, result, execution, and a check status UNDETERMINED. separateAxes keeps authorization, confinement, product and residualLimitation distinct from the outcome, and records that residualLimitation stays 'mandatory and non-nullable. It does not carry the outcome', so nothing is dropped from v4's structure.

The CA-4 unless-bypass is gone. v1 read 'host CA-4 is fail-closed unless explicitly consented and this contract instance exists'. v2's coveredActs.CA-4-host carries no unless clause at all and sets thisContractCannotAdmit: true, and ES-3 states 'No unless-bypass exists' for the unclassified case.

CA-3 subtypes are no longer this-contract-only. subtypeCount is 4 and each subtype carries authorizationRoute, productAdmissionAuthority, sliceSelector, admissionEvidenceToday and standing. OUT_OF_ROOT_READ and LOCAL_SOCKET_OR_PIPE are 'UNOWNED-FOR-ADMISSION… Unexercisable until owner-recorded subtype admission exists', each with admissionEvidenceToday ABSENT and thisContractCannotAdmit true, and each naming the fallback 'a D-000 owner-assignment if the named owners decline'. The four subtypes remain an exact match for BLK-2's four enumerated effects.

KEYCHAIN is fail-closed: authorizationRoute DR-108, productAdmissionAuthority the DR-108 owner, admissionEvidenceToday DEFERRED, standing unexercisable, sliceSelector citing D-002's explicit deferral. It is additionally covered by FC-NOT-SUFFICIENT and by FC-KEYCHAIN's successor class, and effectCommit records its CA-3 commit boundary as 'specified and unused for that subtype' while the deferral holds.

Mints no DR-105 token, and the artifact's own claim about this is exactly true rather than approximately true. It asserts 'Does not mint PT-* tokens. The sole concrete PT-* identifier in this artifact is the out-of-scope reference PT-NET-EGRESS.' Measured: 'PT-' occurs 7 times, of which 5 are PT-NET-EGRESS and the remaining 2 are the literal wildcard 'PT-*' inside that very disclaimer. No other concrete token appears.

No silent SATISFIED: 'SATISFIED' occurs twice, both negative — authorityClaim's 'records nothing as SATISFIED, and authorizes no blueprint', and whatThisDoesNotDo's 'Does not discharge DR-105 or DR-114 SATISFIED.' Header carries status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING. 'WAIV' occurs zero times.

Recited counts are honest: outcomeVocabulary.memberCount 3 against three listed members and against D-032's three; CA-3 subtypeCount 4 against four listed and against BLK-2's four; four covered act families against D-032's enumeration; six fail-closed conjuncts listed and six named in the boolean.

D-032 conformity, checked against the adopted bytes rather than a draft: host-outside-DR-105 at actorSet; consent as an invocation-bound doctor-side record that is not a grant at consent.lifecycle; component tails in DR-105 at ES-2 and coveredActs; necessary-not-sufficient at layers and FC-C4; fail-closed-until-recorded at FC-C1; the three-member outcome minimum at outcomeVocabulary; BLK-3 still routed at joinBlockerDisposition; CA-2 needing DR-119 and DR-117/128 at FC-C6 and coveredActs; the CA-3 routing split at coveredActs.CA-3; permissionRef permanently reserved at outcomeVocabulary.permissionRef; and the egress assignment answered at slice1EgressExecutionSide. All eleven property pins the artifact itself lists are present in its own text.

effectCommit adds a per-class commit boundary — spawn syscall returning a pid, customer-tool process existing, observation syscall issued, first byte handed to the kernel — with reversible-before and irreversible-after marked and the honest consequences drawn: DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED is 'Unlawful after commit, and unlawful when commit-versus-not is unknown', and process death with an unstatable commit yields INDETERMINATE, 'Never refused. Never omitted. Never narrated only in residualLimitation.' That is the anti-mismodeling rule doctor v4 asks for, carried into the successor.

verdictNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES. The v1 REJECT rested on one blocker and it is gone: D-032's single assignment is answered with a rule, the rule is applied, and the bypass it could have left is closed by name. Every one of my three v1 advisories is repaired and two are repaired past what I asked. Neither remaining advisory touches a decision this contract makes; both ask it to disclose something it already reasons its way to — why the DR-105 conjunct does not bind the host half of a member it activates, and how a later reader extracts the section it pins. I record one thing in the artifact's favour that no finding captures: it repairs a defect in its own predecessor by quoting the defective Boolean and stating what still denies, which is the form this corpus asks of a successor and which makes the repair checkable rather than assertable.
